scalar_formula_verification.formula: E[X_+] = E[X]/2 + (1/pi) integral_0^infinity (1 - Re phi_X(t))/t^2 dt
scalar_formula_verification.derivation: Pinelis absolute-moment identity at p=1 gives E|X|=(2/pi) integral (1-Re phi)/t^2; combine with X_+=(X+|X|)/2.

primary_source.title: Positive-part moments via the characteristic functions, and more general expressions

scalar_formula_verification.generalized_joint_embedding_note: Pinelis Theorem 2.3 allows a complex-valued random multiplier Y in generalized positive-part expectations, so scalar positive-part transforms can be embedded in joint expectations.

dense_joint_cf_verification.identity: For Z_j = w_j^T H, phi_Zj(t) = Phi_H(t w_j).
dense_joint_cf_verification.implication: A future arbitrary dense row requires joint-CF information along new row rays; coordinate marginal CFs alone do not determine this generically.

material_corrections.correction: R335 omitted Pilipovsky et al. 2023, a directly relevant published deep-ReLU characteristic-function/Hilbert-transform propagation method.
material_corrections.reason: Its published numerical state is component-wise; its product factorization rule is stated for independent scalar variables, while generic dense hidden coordinates are not generally independent. It does not supply the required generic-dense joint-state, propagated-error, FLOP, or residual guarantees.

material_corrections.correction: R335's explicit orthant decomposition is valid, but explicit 2^n mask enumeration is not proved necessary for every exact representation. Full joint-CF/Hilbert-transform representations can encode the transform without an explicit mask table.
